stem:
The diagram shows transversal $t$ crossing lines $p$ and $q$. Angle $1$ sits above $p$ and to the right of $t$. Angle $2$ sits above $q$ and to the right of $t$.

Which claim about angles $1$ and $2$ is correct?

options.text: Angles $1$ and $2$ are corresponding angles, because each sits in the same matching position at its crossing.
Angles $1$ and $2$ are corresponding angles even when both are taken from the crossing with $p$ alone.
Angles $1$ and $2$ are same-side interior angles, so their measures must sum to $180^{\circ}$.
Angles $1$ and $2$ are corresponding angles only because the printed labels are $1$ and $2$.

teacher.key_rationale: Corresponding angles occupy matching positions at the two crossings of a transversal. Taking both from one line omits that pair condition. Treating them as same-side interior angles conflates a different pair. Echoing the printed labels alone is surface capture.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote parallel-lines source as transversal t on lines p and q with angles 1 and 2 in matching upper-right positions.
